subject: EverGuard: Hosted API — data residency, retention, and deletion follow-up
messages:
From: Evan Miles <evan.miles@everguard.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: EverGuard: Hosted API data residency + retention clarifications

Irene —

Thanks for the quick call earlier. We're putting together our security questionnaire for procurement and a few items need written confirmation for our security team. Can you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted API?

1) Data residency options: can we restrict EverGuard customer data to EU-only or US-only regions for both model input and outputs?
2) Retention defaults: what is the default retention for request/response payloads, logs, and KV/prefix caches? Can we configure shorter retention per tenant?
3) Deletion guarantees: when we request a customer data purge, what systems are purged (runtime caches, live indices, backups, logs) and how long until irrecoverable deletion?
4) Backups & snapshots: do backups ever cross regions? What is retention for snapshots and how are they purged?
5) Evidence: can you provide SOC2 report pointers and a short export showing retention config values for a sample tenant?

We appreciate concise, auditable answers suitable for the questionnaire — we may attach this to our vendor risk tool.

Best,
Evan
Evan Miles
Security Analyst, EverGuard
security@everguard.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: EverGuard: Hosted API data residency + retention clarifications

Evan —

Thanks — answering inline below. I'm attaching a one-page summary and a CSV that maps retention fields to our API/config flags for clarity.

1) Data residency options: Yes. For hosted API customers we offer region scoping at account level. We currently support: "us" (US regions), "eu" (EU regions), and a global option. When an account is scoped to EU, both transient data (request/response payloads, model context) and persistent operational artifacts (billing, audit logs) are stored in EU-region services only. Note: geo-scoping applies to new data after the account is configured; we can assist with migration for existing datasets as part of onboarding.

2) Retention defaults: Default retention on hosted API is: request/response payloads = 30 days; operational logs/traces = 90 days; prefix/KV caches (server-side) = ephemeral — default TTL 1 hour, up to 24 hours depending on workload. Customers can request shorter retention or complete opt-out of retention for request/response data via account settings or a signed DPA amendment. Shorter retentions are enforced at the routing layer and validated by our retention service.

3) Deletion guarantees: On a data purge request we run a multi-stage deletion:
  - Phase 1 (0–24 hours): immediate removal from active runtime caches and any per-request KV entries; tokens and request records become inaccessible via the API.
  - Phase 2 (24–72 hours): deletion from primary object stores (S3 buckets scoped to the account region).
  - Phase 3 (up to 90 days): snapshots/backups retention window (see backups). Backups are rotated and purged per the snapshot lifecycle; when a customer requests irrevocable deletion we schedule snapshot re-encryption and shredding followed by metadata deletion — typically completed within our 90-day window.

We provide an attestation and deletion job id for audit; note that forensically recovering from lower-level infrastructure backups requires coordination with our infra team and is governed by the DPA.

4) Backups & snapshots: Backups are region-scoped and do not cross region boundaries for geo-scoped accounts. Snapshot retention default is 90 days for hosted API; snapshots older than retention are automatically purged. Cross-region replication is not enabled for EU-scoped accounts unless part of an agreed runbook (for DR purposes) and will be documented in the contract.

5) Evidence: Our SOC 2 Type II report and control matrix are available to customers under NDA. I've attached a short PDF summary (redwood-hosted-api-data-retention-summary.pdf) and a CSV export that shows the config flags you asked for (everguard-qa-response-table.csv). If you need the SOC2 artifact we can start an NDA and provide access via the secure portal.

If you want, Rishi can produce the deletion job id flow and Laura can pull the retention-config export for a sandbox tenant so you have a literal sample.

Next steps — tell me if you want a standalone statement we can paste into your questionnaire (short form), or we can hand off the attachments directly into your vendor tool.

Thanks,

Irene Choi
Senior Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

• For deletion job ids, our process wants a consistent format we can reference in our ticketing system. Can Rishi provide an example job id and the API endpoint we would poll for status?

• For EU-scoped accounts — if we later request a cross-region failover for D R testing, how is that handled and would that create copies of data outside EU?

If you can send the sample deletion job id and a short one-paragraph answer for the snapshot metadata question, we can slot this into our vendor portal.

Thanks,
Evan

Evan —

Following up with the specific items you requested. Small, audit-friendly answers below plus an example job id and a polling endpoint.

Snapshot metadata retention:
• We retain minimal snapshot metadata for 365 days to support audit and customer support workflows. Metadata stored: snapshot id, account id (hashed), creation timestamp, retention expiry timestamp. Account ids in metadata are stored as keyed HMAC hashes (pseudonymized) unless otherwise requested in the contract.

Deletion job id example + endpoint:
• Example job id: DJ-20281116-5a7c2f9b
• Polling endpoint (internal API): https://api.redwood.com/internal/v1/deletion-jobs/DJ-20281116-5a7c2f9b/status
  - Response includes status: queued | in_progress | completed | failed, and timestamps for each phase.

EU scoped failover for DR testing:
• Cross-region failover is available as a scheduled DR runbook. It is executed only with customer authorization and is treated as a temporary copy for the duration of the test. Copies are created in the target region and are isolated to a temporary DR account; the copy is shredded after the test unless the customer signs an amendment to enable ongoing replication. Any DR copies are logged and the job id is provided for audit.

Attachments: redwood-hosted-api-data-retention-summary.pdf (short policy) and everguard-qa-response-table.csv (field mappings) — both are attached to this email. We can also drop the CSV into the secure Drive link if you prefer.

If this works, Laura can also produce a sanitized sample export from our sandbox showing fields you can paste into your vendor portal. Want me to create the sanitized export now?
